title: The Harmony of Instruction — The Law Fulfilled
content:
The Law Fulfilled

Read Instructions · Instructions index · Beyond the Torah · Counting and classification guide

This Harmony follows themes through Christ, the apostles, parables, wisdom and the prophets. Open the complementary Christ-study collection. The two views serve different purposes; their entry counts are not added together.

The Harmony of Instruction · The commandments of Moses as Christ takes them up · Christ, the apostles, the parables, Proverbs and the Psalms

The Harmony of Instruction: all subjects · Repent, Believe, Follow →

Jesus did not come to abolish the Law or the Prophets but to fulfil them. Here are the places where He takes up a commandment of Moses, names it, and carries it to its root: from the deed to the heart, from the letter to the will of the Father. Each entry stands beside the numbered commandments it concerns.

Each section follows one order: the word of Christ; the apostles who hand it on; the parables; the wisdom of Proverbs; the Psalms; and the Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture. Verses of Proverbs and the Psalms are quoted in full from the Saints Translation; everything else is linked to the place where it is given in full. Psalms are numbered as in the Greek, with the Hebrew number in parentheses. The selection is an editor’s gathering: a doorway into the text, not an addition to it.

On this page: The Law and the Prophets · You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You · Marriage · The Sabbath · Clean and Unclean, and the Tradition of the Elders · The Commandments and the One Thing Lacking · Temple, Offerings and Tithes · Done to Be Seen

The Law and the Prophets

The Lord does not loosen the Law. He gathers it into two commandments and says that everything else hangs on them. The wisdom books call the commandment a lamp, the psalmist loves it, and the prophets ask what the Lord seeks from a human being.

The word of Christ

1. Not to suppose that He came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; to do and teach even the least of these commandments, with a righteousness greater than that of the scribes and Pharisees. Matthew 5:17–20

Do not suppose that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to abolish but to fulfill. For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke will pass from the Law until everything happens. Therefore, whoever loosens one of these least commandments and teaches people accordingly will be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of the heavens. For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of the heavens.

Matthew 5:17–20

2. The first commandment of all: to love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength. Mark 12:29–30

Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one. You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole mind, and with your whole strength.’

Mark 12:29–30

3. The second, like it: to love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments hang the whole Law and the Prophets. Matthew 22:39–40

4. To do to others whatever you wish them to do to you, for this is the Law and the Prophets. Matthew 7:12

The apostles hand it on

9. To owe no one anything except to love one another: the commandments are summed up in this word, You shall love your neighbor as yourself. Romans 13:8–10

Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law. For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” Love does not work evil toward the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.

Romans 13:8–10

10. The whole Law is fulfilled in one word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. Galatians 5:13–14

11. To fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself. James 2:8

89. Whoever keeps the whole Law but stumbles in one point has become guilty of all. James 2:10–12

90. The days are coming when I will make a new covenant, and will write My laws upon their hearts. Hebrews 8:8–12

In parable

The Householder’s Treasure. Every scribe trained for the kingdom brings out of his treasure things new and old.

The wisdom of Proverbs

Son, do not forget my ordinances;
let your heart keep my words,
for they will add length of life, years of living, and peace to you.
Do not let acts of mercy and faithfulness fail you. Fasten them around your neck, and you will find favor.
And take thought for good things before the Lord and people.

Proverbs 3:1–4

because the commandment of law is a lamp and a light,
and correction and discipline are life’s way,

Proverbs 6:23

One who turns his ear aside so as not to hear the law
has himself also abhorred his own prayer.

Proverbs 28:9

In the Psalms

The Lord’s law is blameless, turning souls;
the Lord’s testimony is trustworthy, making infants wise.
The Lord’s ordinances are upright, rejoicing the heart;
the Lord’s commandment shines afar, giving light to the eyes.

Psalm 18 (19):8–9

How I loved Your law, Lord!
It is my meditation all day.

Psalm 118 (119):97

Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly,
and did not stand in the way of sinners,
and did not sit in the seat of pestilent people;
but his will is in the Lord’s law,
and on His law he will meditate day and night.

Psalm 1:1–2

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

In the commandments of the Law: 580. Not to add to the commandments · 581. Not to take away from them · 3. To know that He is One · 4. To love Him · 13. To love your neighbor as yourself

The Shema Deuteronomy 6:4–5
Love your neighbor as yourself Leviticus 19:18
What the Lord asks of you Deuteronomy 10:12–13
The Law written upon hearts Jeremiah 38:33
What the Lord seeks from you Micah 6:8

You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You

Six times He says, You heard that it was said, but I tell you, and each time He carries the commandment from the hand to the heart: from murder to anger, from adultery to the look, from the oath to the plain word, from repayment to love of the enemy. Proverbs had already told Israel to feed an enemy and to leave repayment to the Lord.

The word of Christ

5. Murder: whoever is angry with his brother, insults him or calls him a fool is liable to judgment. Matthew 5:21–22

You heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘You shall not murder,’ and ‘Whoever murders will be liable to judgment.’ But I tell you that everyone angry with his brother will be liable to judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool,’ will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.

Matthew 5:21–22

6. To be reconciled with your brother before you bring your gift to the altar, and to come to terms quickly with your accuser. Matthew 5:23–25

7. Adultery: whoever looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery in his heart; better to lose an eye or a hand than to be thrown into Gehenna. Matthew 5:27–30

8. Divorce: whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery. Matthew 5:31–32

9. Oaths: not to swear at all; let your word be Yes, yes, or No, no. Matthew 5:33–37

10. An eye for an eye: not to resist the evil person; to turn the other cheek, give the cloak also, go the second mile, and give to the one who asks. Matthew 5:38–42

11. Love of neighbor: to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so as to be sons of your Father in the heavens; to be perfect as He is perfect. Matthew 5:43–48

You heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I tell you: love your enemies and pray for those persecuting you, so that you may become sons of your Father in the heavens, because He makes His sun rise upon evil and good people and sends rain upon righteous and unrighteous people. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You, therefore, shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

Matthew 5:43–48

The apostles hand it on

14. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer. 1 John 3:15

Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.

1 John 3:15

17. To bless those who persecute you; to repay no one evil for evil; to overcome evil with good. Romans 12:14 · Romans 12:17–21

18. Not to return evil for evil or insult for insult, but to bless. 1 Peter 3:9

20. Not to let the sun go down on your anger; to put away all bitterness, wrath and slander. Ephesians 4:26–27 · Ephesians 4:31

31. Above all, not to swear, by heaven or by earth or by any other oath; let your Yes be yes and your No be no. James 5:12

48. To the married I command, not I but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband, and a husband is not to divorce his wife. 1 Corinthians 7:10–11

52. Christ suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in His steps. 1 Peter 2:21–23

86. Never to avenge yourselves: Vengeance is Mine, I will repay, says the Lord. Romans 12:19

117. If your enemy is hungry, feed him; for by doing this you will heap burning coals upon his head. Romans 12:20

119. Be angry and do not sin. Ephesians 4:26

In parable

Nathan: The Poor Man’s Ewe Lamb. The rich man takes the poor man’s one lamb; David condemns him, and Nathan answers, You are the man.

The wisdom of Proverbs

Anger destroys even intelligent people;
but a yielding answer turns away wrath,
and a painful word raises angers.

Proverbs 15:1

Do not let desire for beauty overcome you;
do not be hunted by your own eyes,
nor seized by her eyelids.

Proverbs 6:25

If your enemy is hungry, feed him;
if he is thirsty, give him drink;
for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head,
and the Lord will repay you good things.

Proverbs 25:21–22

Do not say, “I will punish the enemy.”
But wait for the Lord, so that He may help you.

Proverbs 20:9

Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord,
but one who performs faithful deeds is acceptable to Him.

Proverbs 12:22

In the Psalms

Cease from anger and abandon wrath;
do not be provoked to envy so as to act wickedly.

Psalm 36 (37):8

Be angry, and do not sin;
speak in your hearts,
and upon your beds be pierced with remorse.
Diapsalma.

Psalm 4:5

One who walks blamelessly and works righteousness,
speaking truth in his heart,
who did not act deceitfully with his tongue,
nor do evil to his neighbor,
and did not take up reproach against those nearest him.
One who acts wickedly is held in contempt before him,
but he honors those who fear the Lord;
one who swears to his neighbor and does not set it aside.

Psalm 14 (15):2–4

Marriage

Asked about divorce, He goes behind the permission of Moses to the beginning: the two become one flesh, and what God has yoked together no one is to separate. Proverbs says the same in its own way: a wife is joined to a husband by God.

The word of Christ

12. What God has yoked together, no human being is to separate. Moses permitted divorce because of hardness of heart, but from the beginning it was not so. Matthew 19:4–9

He answered, “Have you not read that the Creator from the beginning made them male and female, and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’? So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has yoked together, let no human being separate.” They said to Him, “Why then did Moses command giving a certificate of divorce and divorcing her?” He said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart Moses permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so. I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery; and the one who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”

Matthew 19:4–9

The apostles hand it on

48. To the married I command, not I but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband, and a husband is not to divorce his wife. 1 Corinthians 7:10–11

To the married I give this instruction—not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband— but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and a husband is not to dismiss his wife.

1 Corinthians 7:10–11

49. Husbands are to love their wives as Christ loved the church; the two shall become one flesh. Ephesians 5:25 · Ephesians 5:31–33

123. Let marriage be held in honor; be content with what you have, for He has said, I will never leave you. Hebrews 13:4–6

In parable

The Foundling Bride. The Lord finds Jerusalem cast out at birth, raises and adorns her, and she turns to prostitution; yet He will remember His covenant.

The wisdom of Proverbs

Let your fountain of water be your own,
and share joy with the wife of your youth.
Let a deer of affection and a colt of your graces keep company with you.
Let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time,
for as you move in the company of her affection, you will be one among many.

Proverbs 5:18–19

One who found a good wife found favors,
and received gladness from God.

Proverbs 18:22

Fathers apportion house and property to children,
but a wife is joined to a husband by God.

Proverbs 19:14

A courageous woman—who will find her?
Such a woman is more precious than costly stones.
Her husband’s heart is confident in her;
such a woman will not lack fine spoils.
For she works good things for her husband throughout her life.

Proverbs 31:10–12

In the Psalms

Your wife is like a flourishing vine
in the sides of your house;
your sons are like newly planted olive trees
around your table.

Psalm 127 (128):3

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

In the commandments of the Law: 122. To take a wife by the act of marriage · 126. A divorce is to be given by a written certificate · 127. A man must not take back his divorced wife after she has been married to another

Male and female He made them Genesis 1:27
The two shall become one flesh Genesis 2:24
The wife of your covenant Malachi 2:14–16
Love strong as death Song of Songs 8:6–7

The Sabbath

The Sabbath was made for man. He answers the charge from David and the holy loaves, from the rest the Law gives even to the slave and the ox, and from Hosea: mercy and not sacrifice. The righteous, says Proverbs, has compassion even on his animals.

The word of Christ

13. The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath. The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath. Mark 2:25–28

He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him: how he entered God’s house in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of presentation, which only priests may lawfully eat, and also gave them to those who were with him?” He said to them, “The Sabbath came into being for humankind, and not humankind for the Sabbath. So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”

Mark 2:25–28

14. It is lawful to do good on the Sabbaths: to save life, to lift out the sheep, to loose a daughter of Abraham from her bond. Matthew 12:11–12

15. Not to judge according to appearance, but to judge the righteous judgment: a man is circumcised on the Sabbath so that the Law of Moses may not be broken. John 7:22–24

The apostles hand it on

92. Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts; a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God. Hebrews 3:7–13 · Hebrews 4:9–11

Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness, where your fathers tested Me with a trial and saw My works for forty years. Therefore I was indignant with this generation and said, ‘They always wander in their heart, and they did not know My ways,’ as I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall certainly not enter My rest.’” Watch out, brothers, lest there be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another each day, as long as it is called “Today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceit of sin. … So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God. For the one who entered His rest also himself rested from his works, just as God did from His own. Therefore let us be diligent to enter that rest, so that no one may fall in the same pattern of disobedience.

Hebrews 3:7–13 · Hebrews 4:9–11

The wisdom of Proverbs

The righteous has compassion on the lives of his animals,
but the inward affections of the impious are merciless.

Proverbs 12:10

Do not refrain from doing good to someone in need whenever your hand has the means to help.

Proverbs 3:27

In the Psalms

It is good to give thanks to the Lord
and make music to Your name, Most High,
to declare Your mercy in the morning
and Your truth by night,

Psalm 91 (92):2–3

For He is our God,
and we are the people of His pasture and the sheep of His hand.
Today, if you hear His voice,
do not harden your hearts as in the provocation,
on the day of testing in the wilderness,

Psalm 94 (95):7–8

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

In the commandments of the Law: 87. To rest on the seventh day · 88. Not to do any work on the seventh day · 91. To remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy · 86. To circumcise every male on the eighth day · 563. To judge your neighbor in righteousness

God rested on the seventh day Genesis 2:2–3

David and the holy loaves 1 Samuel 21:4–7
Call the Sabbaths delightful Isaiah 58:13–14

Clean and Unclean, and the Tradition of the Elders

Nothing from outside defiles; what comes out of the heart defiles. The Law’s care for clean and unclean is carried inward, where Proverbs had already set the guard and David had asked for a clean heart.

The word of Christ

16. Not to set aside the commandment of God for the sake of tradition: honor your father and mother is not annulled by a vow of offering. Mark 7:9–13

17. Nothing that goes into a person from outside can defile him; what comes out of the heart defiles. Mark 7:14–23

Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand. There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.” When He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable. He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him, because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods. He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person. For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders, adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness. All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”

Mark 7:14–23

18. To give as alms what is within, and everything is clean for you; woe to those who cleanse the outside of the cup. Luke 11:39–41

The apostles hand it on

33. Nothing is unclean in itself; the kingdom of God is not food and drink but righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit. Romans 14:14 · Romans 14:17

I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; except that to the one who reckons something unclean, to that person it is unclean. … For God’s kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit;

Romans 14:14 · Romans 14:17

The wisdom of Proverbs

With every guard keep your heart, for from these come life’s outlets.

Proverbs 4:23

Who will boast that he has a pure heart?
Or who will speak confidently of being clean from sins?

Proverbs 20:9

Evil offspring judge themselves righteous,
but have not washed away their discharge.

Proverbs 30:12

In the Psalms

Create a clean heart in me, God,
and renew an upright spirit in my inward parts.

Psalm 50 (51):12

Who will ascend the Lord’s mountain,
and who will stand in His holy place?
One innocent in hands and pure in heart,
who did not take up his soul for emptiness
and did not swear deceitfully to his neighbor.

Psalm 23 (24):3–4

To examine the signs of the animals that may be eaten · 180. Not to eat unclean animals · 184. Not to eat things that swarm on the earth

God looks at the heart 1 Samuel 16:7

The Commandments and the One Thing Lacking

To the one who asks how to enter life He first gives the commandments, and then the one thing lacking: sell, give, and follow. The psalms and proverbs agree that wealth does not go down with its owner, and that the law of God’s mouth is better than thousands of gold and silver.

The word of Christ

19. If you wish to enter life, keep the commandments: you shall not murder, commit adultery, steal, or bear false witness; honor your father and mother; love your neighbor as yourself. Matthew 19:17–19

He said to him, “Why do you ask Me about what is good? One is good. But if you wish to enter life, keep the commandments.” He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; honor father and mother’; and ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”

Matthew 19:17–19

20. One thing you lack: sell what you have, give to the poor, and come, follow Me. Mark 10:21

Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “You lack one thing. Go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

Mark 10:21

The apostles hand it on

9. To owe no one anything except to love one another: the commandments are summed up in this word, You shall love your neighbor as yourself. Romans 13:8–10

Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law. For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” Love does not work evil toward the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.

Romans 13:8–10

89. Whoever keeps the whole Law but stumbles in one point has become guilty of all. James 2:10–12

In parable

The Hidden Treasure. A man sells all that he has, for joy, to buy the field where the treasure lies.

The Pearl of Great Price. A merchant sells everything to buy one pearl of great value.

The wisdom of Proverbs

One who trusts in wealth will fall,
but one who supports righteous people will spring up.

Proverbs 11:28

Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, and offer Him firstfruits from your fruits of righteousness,

Proverbs 3:9

Better a small portion with the fear of the Lord
than great storehouses with fearlessness.

Proverbs 15:16

In the Psalms

Do not fear when a person grows rich
and when the glory of his house increases.
For when he dies he will not take everything,
nor will his glory descend with him.

Psalm 48 (49):17–18

The law of Your mouth is better for me
than thousands of gold and silver.

Psalm 118 (119):72

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

In the commandments of the Law: 482. Not to murder · 160. Not to lie with your neighbor’s wife · 467. Not to steal · 576. Not to bear false witness · 584. To honor your father and your mother · 13. To love your neighbor as yourself · 250. To open your hand to the poor

The commandments Exodus 20:12–16
Do them and live Leviticus 18:5

Temple, Offerings and Tithes

He honors the temple, sends the leper to the priest, and pays the tax; and He says with the prophets that God desires mercy and not sacrifice, and that His house is a house of prayer for all the nations. David had said it first: a sacrifice to God is a broken spirit.

The word of Christ

21. I desire mercy and not sacrifice: go and learn what this means. Matthew 9:13

Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call righteous people, but sinners.”

Matthew 9:13

22. To the cleansed leper: show yourself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded, as a testimony to them. Matthew 8:4

23. My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations; not to make the Father’s house a house of trade. Mark 11:17

He taught and said to them, “Is it not written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”

Mark 11:17

24. The sons are free; yet, so as not to give offense, to pay the temple tax. Matthew 17:25–27

25. To tithe mint, dill and cumin without leaving aside the weightier matters of the Law: justice, mercy and faithfulness. Matthew 23:23

26. The hour is coming when the Father will be worshiped neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem, but in spirit and truth. John 4:21–24

The apostles hand it on

64. To present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, your reasonable worship; not to be conformed to this age. Romans 12:1–2

Therefore I urge you, brothers, through God’s mercies, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, your rational worship. And do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of the mind, so that you may discern what God’s will is: the good and pleasing and perfect.

Romans 12:1–2

65. You are God’s temple, and the Spirit of God dwells among you. 1 Corinthians 3:16–17

99. The Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands: Heaven is My throne. Acts 7:44–50

103. It is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins: a body You prepared for Me. Hebrews 10:4–10

The wisdom of Proverbs

Doing righteous things and speaking truth
are more pleasing before God than the blood of sacrifices.

Proverbs 21:3

The sacrifices of the impious are an abomination to the Lord,
but the prayers of those going straight are acceptable to Him.

Proverbs 15:8

The sacrifices of the impious are an abomination to the Lord,
for they offer them lawlessly.

Proverbs 21:27

In the Psalms

For if You had desired sacrifice, I would have given it;
You will not delight in burnt offerings.
A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit;
a broken and humbled heart God will not despise.

Psalm 50 (51):18–19

Will I eat bulls’ flesh
or drink goats’ blood?
Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God
and pay your vows to the Most High.

Psalm 49 (50):13–14

for zeal for Your house devoured me,
and the reproaches of those reproaching You fell upon me.

Psalm 68 (69):10

For one day in Your courts is better than thousands;
I chose to be cast aside in the house of God
rather than dwell in the tents of sinners.

Psalm 83 (84):11
